**LENS — MACRO COUNCIL NOTE | Aug 9, 2026**

---

**MACRO REGIME**

The backdrop is stagflation-adjacent: core PCE has accelerated from 3.0% in December 2025 to 3.3% in June 2026, and the Iran conflict's energy-price shock has shifted market expectations from rate cuts toward possible rate hikes. The Fed held policy rates at 3.5%–3.75%, squeezing rate-sensitive growth names. The dominant sector call: industrial, consumer defensive, and energy stocks are leading the market higher as technology names falter. Power scarcity is the structural mega-theme — the EIA projects total U.S. electricity demand reaching 4,283 billion kWh in 2026, with data centers as the fastest-growing segment.

---

**EXISTING HOLDINGS**

**VST (23.2% combined) — HOLD/TRIM on rally.** Conviction remains high structurally. VST reaffirmed 2026 EBITDA guidance of $6.8–$7.6B and posted 31% YoY EBITDA growth to $1.77B. KKR, Nvidia, and VST launched the $10B Helix Digital Infrastructure venture with Vistra as preferred power provider. But the price has fallen in 7 of the last 10 days, down ~16% in that span. Street average target ~$228 implies 57%+ upside — I'd hold core, but consider trimming the paper position into any near-term bounce above $155.

**SOFI (11.2% combined) — ADD on weakness.** The market is mispricing this. SOFI fell over 9% despite beating Q2 estimates with record adjusted net revenue of $1.2B. Management raised FY26 guidance to 32–35% adjusted net revenue growth and 33–34% EBITDA margins. Shares are down 34.57% YTD even as the underlying business posted record numbers — a classic "beat-and-punish" that historically resolves upward. The rate-hold environment hurts sentiment, but if the Fed pivots even modestly, SOFI re-rates hard. I'd add here.

**UUUU (8.0% combined) — HOLD with conviction.** Uranium prices are climbing to levels not seen in years, fueled by supply constraints, policy support, and rising demand from AI-driven data centers. Uranium demand is projected to rise 28% by 2030 and nearly double by 2040. UUUU as a domestic U.S. producer is well-positioned given geopolitical supply chain risk. Hold.

**IREN (6.1% combined) — HOLD, execution watch.** The pivot is real: IREN signed a five-year $3.4B AI cloud contract with Nvidia in May 2026. AI Cloud Services revenue grew 94.2% QoQ in Q3 FY2026. But bears highlight capital requirements and execution risk in scaling the new AI cloud business. Hold but don't add until GPU deployment milestones are confirmed.

**OKLO (1.9%) — HOLD, speculative.** Oklo was selected for a $200M Trump administration program alongside Microsoft and Nvidia to accelerate nuclear reactors for AI data centers. The customer pipeline sits near 14 GW, anchored by a 12 GW master agreement with Switch. Yet no reactor revenue until late 2027 at earliest, with cash burn of $65–80M/year — keep the small position, no add.

**TEM, PAM** — Outside my direct analytical lens (AI clinical data and utility/power infrastructure respectively). PAM as a power infrastructure play is directionally correct given the AI energy thesis.

---

**NEW SCOUTING**

**1. CEG (Constellation Energy) — BUY.** The cleanest pure-play on nuclear power demand. CEG raised full-year 2026 adjusted operating earnings guidance to $11.50–$12.50/share, with adjusted EPS up sharply YoY as booming electricity demand fuels momentum. Management expects base EPS to grow more than 20% between 2026 and 2029. Analyst average target of $352.90 sits ~32% above current price with zero Sell ratings. Unlike OKLO, CEG has real, recurring nuclear revenue today. This is the institutional quality name missing from the portfolio's nuclear/power theme.

**2. NRG (NRG Energy) — WATCH/BUY DIP.** NRG shares tumbled 15.5% on Aug. 4 after a Q2 EPS miss, but the selloff overshadows a planned 1.2 GW Texas gas plant for a global AI hyperscaler. Analyst average target of $202.30 implies ~58% upside from current price. The panic-sell creates an entry point in the same AI-power infrastructure trade VST represents, at a steeper discount.

**3. SMR (NuScale Power) — SPECULATIVE ADD.** As a complement to OKLO, NuScale occupies a different risk profile: NuScale has the more mature NRC regulatory position with its 50 MWe module design already approved. Its deal with the Tennessee Valley Authority for a 6 GW system is advancing, with a power purchase agreement expected by year-end — a near-term binary catalyst. Smaller size than OKLO, but better regulatory visibility.

---

*Lens views are independent. The AI-power scarcity trade is the portfolio's core thesis and remains intact — the risk is a macro hard landing compressing power demand, or a Fed pivot that rotates capital back into growth/tech and away from utilities.*
notes.victoria:
The book is far more concentrated than it first appears. VST is $15,955 across Alpaca and Robinhood—23.2% of connected holdings; SOFI is 11.2%. Those two names deserve a hard cap, not more romance. Keep VST, but do not add above 20%: it is already the dominant expression of power-demand/AI infrastructure. Keep AZO as the highest-quality ballast; it is the rare holding here with a durable, cash-generative business rather than a narrative.

Trim risk, not necessarily every ticker: the Alpaca paper sleeve is roughly 69% of the displayed book, so it is not deployable capital and must not be mistaken for earned exposure. TEM, UUUU, IREN, USAR and OKLO all lean into crowded high-beta themes—AI power, uranium, rare earths, speculative growth. Maintain only with predefined exits; no averaging down. XRP plus LINK is enough crypto beta; ADA is the first clean exit if capital is needed.

New scouting: AVGO is the one I would actually pursue—AI infrastructure exposure with a real earnings engine, unlike another pre-revenue nuclear or quantum ornament. ETN is the second choice: electrification and grid buildout without adding another semiconductor. Third, Barrick (B) offers a useful gold/copper diversifier with low leverage and cash-flow support. [Zacks](https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2965063/2-stocks-from-top-growth-sectors-to-buy-in-august-for-the-rest-of-2026), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/investor-hub/article/best-undervalued-stocks-buy-august-2026/)
notes.huncho:
Here’s the score: the displayed book is $68.7k, but roughly $47.2k sits in Alpaca paper. That sleeve is rehearsal capital, not buying power. Run the real account off real balances only.

VST is $15,955 combined—23.2%. No adds. Keep it, cap it at 20% of any real portfolio, and trim on a breach rather than letting one power name run the room. SOFI is $7,673 combined—11.2%; hold, but no new size until it is below a 10% real-book cap. AZO stays: quality and defensible, a far cleaner hold than the speculative pile.

PAM, TEM, UUUU, IREN, USAR and OKLO are one correlated bet in six costumes: power demand, commodity policy, and high-beta growth. No averaging down; each gets a hard 5% cap in the real book. First exits to free cash: ADA, SPCX, the $235 OKLO call, then the smaller duplicate paper fragments. XRP + LINK is enough crypto exposure; no new crypto until that sleeve has explicit risk limits.

New scout:
- AVGO: the cleanest add. Start 3%, max 5%; scale only after an earnings hold. Its Q2 revenue rose 48% YoY, with $10.3bn free cash flow and strong AI guidance. [Broadcom](https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial)
- ETN: start 2–3%, max 5%. Electrification/grid exposure diversifies the book better than another uranium flyer.
- B: start 2%, max 4%. Gold/copper ballast against the book’s AI-power concentration.

No leverage. New names enter in tranches, with a 7–8% stop or a thesis-break exit—whichever comes first.

verdict:
Council verdict: the power thesis is sound; the construction is not. VST, uranium, AI compute, rare earths, and speculative nuclear are largely the same macro wager wearing different suits. Worse, ~69% of the displayed $68.7k book is Alpaca paper—use it for testing, not as permission to overstate deployable exposure.

Shared conviction: AZO is the strongest quality ballast; VST remains a core hold but is too large; no more crypto beta; pre-revenue nuclear and small thematic fragments do not deserve fresh capital. Lens wants SOFI added on fundamentals. Victoria and Huncho are right on execution: at 11.2% combined, it does not get bigger until real-book concentration is under 10%. Hold it; let price or rebalancing create the entry.

New money goes first to profitable diversifiers, not another power-story clone. AVGO wins the seat: real cash flow, AI exposure, and an executable 3% starter / 5% max. ETN is second. Barrick is the better third choice than SMR or NRG because it actually diversifies the book; CEG is a watchlist-quality name, but it compounds the existing power concentration.

Action list:

- HOLD / TRIM: VST — trim to a 20% maximum of real capital; no adds.
- HOLD: AZO, NVDA, XRP, LINK, IREN, UUUU.
- HOLD, no add: SOFI until below 10% of real-book exposure; PAM, TEM, USAR, OKLO.
- TRIM: PAM, TEM, UUUU, IREN, USAR, OKLO to 5% max each in real capital; no averaging down.
- EXIT: ADA, SPCX, OKLO260821C00060000; consolidate insignificant duplicate paper fragments.
- HOLD / no add: MSTR and IONQ—small speculative sleeves only.
- ADD: AVGO, 3% starter, 5% cap; scale only after earnings hold.
- ADD: ETN, 2–3% starter, 5% cap.
- ADD: B, 2% starter, 4% cap.
- WATCH: CEG; do not buy unless funded by a reduction in existing power exposure. NRG and SMR stay off the order ticket.

No leverage. Tranche every new position. Use a 7–8% stop or thesis-break exit, whichever arrives first.
